name: Anselm's Mercy

sorting.name: The Sorting Deck
sorting.desc: Triage, in the old shuttle bay. Everyone who comes aboard gets a colored tag here, and the color decides nearly everything after that.

W.label: Dr. Adeyemi
asks: How many did you lose last night, Doctor?

t.name: The triage table
t.look: A steel table, a pen on a string, and a stack of forms. It's worn pale at the spot where someone has been leaning on it for months.
t.use: I stand at the triage table for a while and watch how it's done.

g.name: A box of colored tags
g.look: Red, amber, green and grey, sorted by a careful hand. The grey box is the fullest, and nobody on the deck will look straight at it.
g.use: I pick a grey tag out of the box and ask what it means.

k.name: A crash cart
k.look: The last well-stocked cart on the deck, with a trauma kit strapped to the top. The tally on its lid is in three different hands, and they don't agree.
k.use: I ask whether anyone can spare a trauma kit off the crash cart.

ward.name: The Long Ward
ward.desc: A converted cargo hold, with row upon row of cots and families sleeping underneath them. Ward Six is at the far end.

P.label: Pavel
asks: How are you feeling today, Pavel?
Do you remember anything from before you woke up?
P.greeting: {name} looks up from a heap of potatoes, delighted to see anyone at all.

d.name: Drawings over a warning label
d.look: Crayon suns and crayon ships, taped over the hazard stencils. Under one of them you can still read FLAMMABLE. Under another, somebody's drawn the Meridian.
d.use: I stop to look at the children's drawings, and ask who drew the Meridian.

l.name: A surgeon's lens
l.look: A jeweler's eyepiece rebuilt for field surgery, left on a cot rail by somebody who was called away in a hurry. It's a very good one.
l.use: I pick up the surgeon's lens and go looking for whoever left it.

q.name: An empty cot in Ward Six
q.look: It was made up fresh this morning. Lately, a lot of the cots at this end of the ward have needed making up, and not for the usual reason.
q.use: I ask the nurse who was in this cot, and where they've gone.

still.name: The Still Ward
still.desc: A dim, peaceful compartment for the comatose. There are eleven beds, and they've all been full since the Fall.

m.name: The monitors
m.look: Eleven heart monitors, all ticking along very quietly. You stand there longer than you meant to before you work out what's bothering you about them.
m.use: I watch the monitors for a few minutes, with a nurse's log beside me.

c.name: The night nurse's chair
c.look: A plain chair in the middle of the room, with a folded blanket on it and a smooth silver token left on the blanket. Whoever sits here has a good view of all eleven, and nothing to do.
c.use: I sit down in the night nurse's chair, and I turn the silver token over.

b.name: The power board
b.look: Hand-labeled breakers, and a note that says what this room costs per day in a very small hand. Somebody has underlined it, and somebody else has rubbed that out.
b.use: I read the power board and ask who signs off on this ward.

stair.name: The Bell Stair
stair.desc: A stairwell with a salvaged ship's bell at the top, rung by anyone well enough to walk out. You can hear it on every deck.

b.name: The bell
b.look: A salvaged ship's bell, with the name of a ship nobody remembers filed off it. The rope's been worn smooth by very few hands. It's been rung eleven times since Aurelis.
b.use: I put my hand on the bell rope and ask who rang it last.

n.name: Notches on the rail
n.look: Eleven notches cut into the handrail, each one different, each with a set of initials beside it. There's room for a twelfth, and somebody's already marked the spot.
n.use: I run my thumb along the notches, and ask the nearest patient who they were.

gallery.name: The Gallery
gallery.desc: The upper walkway, where visiting families camp and trade: places in the queue, blood chits, laundry hours and news. Almost nothing up here is legal, and the nurses need all of it.

T.label: Tessaly
asks: What's in the bag, Doctor Marsh?
Who are you selling to these days?

b.name: A slate of blood chits
b.look: A going rate for a pint, chalked up like the price of beans, and a queue of people with their sleeves already rolled.
b.use: I ask what a pint of blood will buy up here today.

s.name: A very long sweater
s.look: A child's sweater, eleven meters long and still growing, in every color of wool the ship has had. The knitter nods politely and doesn't stop.
s.use: I sit down with the woman knitting the long sweater, and ask about it.

k.name: A medkit on a blanket
k.look: A proper sealed medkit, offered for trade on a square of blanket. It's got a hospital stamp on it, and the seller has put their thumb over the stamp.
k.use: I ask what the seller wants for the medkit, and where it came from.

q.name: A loose strip of calm tabs
q.look: Calm tabs, sold singly, for laundry hours. It's the cheapest thing on the Gallery, and the first to run out each day.
q.use: I trade for a strip of calm tabs.
